gml:Dictionary.gml:description: Codes for action taken to address the CAUSE of a non-conformance so that it does not recur, used for the value of the correctiveAction property of diggs:NonConformance. Deliberately distinct from disposition on the same object, which concerns what happens to the affected work itself; recording only one of the two is common, but conflating them loses a distinction a reviewer needs. Repeatable, since one finding commonly triggers more than one change. Not to be confused with diggs:RIColumnConstruction/groutLevelCorrectiveAction, which is a narrow, in-progress, rigid-inclusion-specific response to one failure mode rather than a systemic change. Built at W3 - see docs/build/W3/NOTES.md. PROVISIONAL pending SME review.
gml:Dictionary.gml:name: DIGGS Non-conformance Corrective Action Codelist Definitions

diggs:Definition.gml:description: The construction method or written procedure was revised - a different drilling or grouting technique, a changed tooling configuration, or an amended method statement.
diggs:Definition.gml:name: Installation method change

diggs:Definition.gml:description: The controlling process parameters were adjusted - grout pressure or volume, penetration rate, rotation speed, withdrawal rate - without changing the method itself. The revised targets belong in the governing specification; this code records only that they changed in response to the finding.
diggs:Definition.gml:name: Control parameter adjustment

diggs:Definition.gml:description: Plant was repaired, recalibrated, or exchanged for a different rig, pump, or tool because the equipment was found to have caused or contributed to the departure.
diggs:Definition.gml:name: Equipment change

diggs:Definition.gml:description: The order or spacing of installation was revised - for example increasing the offset to freshly installed elements, or the minimum age before an adjacent element is installed.
diggs:Definition.gml:name: Installation sequence change

diggs:Definition.gml:description: Verification was intensified - a higher testing density, additional hold or witness points, or a test type added that was not previously required.
diggs:Definition.gml:name: Increased testing or inspection

diggs:Definition.gml:description: Additional or more senior site supervision was put in place, without a change to the method or the testing regime.
diggs:Definition.gml:name: Increased supervision

diggs:Definition.gml:description: Operators or supervisors were retrained or reinstructed where the cause was found to be execution rather than method or plant.
diggs:Definition.gml:name: Personnel training

diggs:Definition.gml:description: The material, mix, or supplier was changed - a revised grout mix, a different aggregate source, or a changed reinforcement supplier.
diggs:Definition.gml:name: Material or supply change

diggs:Definition.gml:description: The design or its ground-model assumptions were re-examined because the departure suggested the premise, rather than the execution, was at fault. Where the review changed the requirement, the disposition is redesign.
diggs:Definition.gml:name: Design review

diggs:Definition.gml:description: The cause was investigated and found isolated, so no systemic change was made. Recorded explicitly rather than by omitting the element, so that an investigated-and-closed finding is distinguishable from one where the cause was never examined.
diggs:Definition.gml:name: No corrective action
